plugins.description: Turns Kalinka Player into an AirPlay speaker, so an iPhone, iPad or Mac can play to it. Works with AirPlay 2 and classic AirPlay. Not made or endorsed by Apple.
plugins.name: AirPlay

notes: Requires Kalinka Player server 5.9.0 or newer (below 6.0.0), which brings plugin SDK 3.11, and a Kalinka Player renderer 0.5.0 or newer (below 1.0.0) with live stream support. The audio plays through the renderer selected in Kalinka Player, on this or another machine; the server itself opens no audio hardware.

Each stream is encoded at the sender's own sample rate and bit depth: 16-bit 44.1 kHz for classic AirPlay and AirPlay 2 realtime streams, 24-bit 48 kHz for Apple Music Lossless over AirPlay 2. Kalinka Player names the codec as FLAC, the lossless carrier to the renderer, whatever the sender used.

The package bundles shairport-sync 5.5.2 with AirPlay 2 and nqptp 1.2.8, built against Debian 13's libraries, which apt checks on install. It installs on Debian 13 and on 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS 13 or DietPi based on it, on amd64 or arm64; a 32-bit userspace does not qualify.
The package also requires flac and coreutils (GNU stdbuf), which apt installs for unbuffered delivery of encoded audio to the Kalinka Player renderer.

AirPlay 2 needs UDP ports 319 and 320 for nqptp; the package grants the server CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE for it. Keep a distribution shairport-sync or nqptp service disabled. When the ports are taken, classic AirPlay is offered instead. A firewall must allow UDP 5353, TCP 7000, UDP 319-320 and 6000-6009, and the ephemeral range 32768-60999 over TCP and UDP.

This independent integration is not certified or endorsed by Apple. Remote control from Kalinka Player (pause, play, next, previous) reaches classic AirPlay senders only; AirPlay 2 senders are controlled from the sending device.

plugins.description: Runs Roon Bridge on the server, so Roon can play to the DAC connected to it. Kalinka Player shows what Roon is playing, with cover art and progress. You need a Roon Server and a Roon subscription. Roon Bridge is downloaded from Roon Labs when you turn the plugin on. Not Roon Ready certified or endorsed by Roon Labs.
plugins.name: Roon Bridge

notes: A Roon Server and a Roon subscription are required. Enabling the plugin downloads Roon Labs' proprietary Roon Bridge for this machine, or attaches to the audio endpoint of a Roon Server already running on it; this integration is not Roon Ready certified or endorsed by Roon Labs.
Requires Kalinka Player server 5.6.0 or newer (below 6.0.0), which brings SDK 3.7 and the external playback API. The package depends on Node.js 18 or newer, which apt installs with it.

Roon plays straight to the server's local DAC and bypasses the Kalinka Player renderer; Kalinka Player shows what plays and keeps Roon's session across pause. The Kalinka Player volume slider controls the Roon output only on a server with external-volume support (plugin SDK 3.11 or newer); released servers up to 5.8.0 ship older SDKs and keep playback without Roon volume.
Initial distro allowlist is conservative: Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04. Derivatives must match an explicitly listed OS identity.

plugins.description: Browse TIDAL Home, Explore, Genres, Moods, your mixes and your collection, search for music, and play supported streams in Kalinka Player. Sign in with your TIDAL account; playback requires a subscription. Uses the unofficial tidalapi client and is not made or endorsed by TIDAL.
plugins.name: TIDAL

notes: Requires Kalinka Player server 5.13.0 or newer (below 6), which brings plugin SDK 3.16, and Python 3.11 or newer. AAC, MP4 and segmented streams play on renderer 0.10.0 or newer.

Sign in by approving this player at the TIDAL link in plugin settings; Kalinka Player connects automatically. If TIDAL ends the session, plugin settings warn that the sign-in expired and offer a new link. Playback requires a TIDAL streaming subscription; availability depends on the account and region.

Maximum audio quality offers Lossless (16-bit / 44.1 kHz) and Max (up to 24-bit / 192 kHz). Plays direct and segmented FLAC, AAC and MP3 streams; TIDAL chooses the codec, and may return AAC for a lossless request. Encrypted streams and Dolby Atmos are refused. TIDAL collections are read-only.

The architecture-independent DEB is built and tested on Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 for ARM64 and amd64. A compatible Debian-packaged Kalinka Player server and resolvable Python dependencies are required.
This integration uses the unofficial tidalapi client. Automated tests use fake API responses.
To change accounts, turn on Unlink Tidal in plugin settings and apply and restart, then sign in again.
